answer_1.quote: In this paper, we explore the task of Recipe-Grounded Conversation, where the dialogue agent is expected to converse with a user to walk him/her through the cooking procedure of a recipe, while answering any questions that might arise along the way

answer_2.quote: We report the following automatic evaluation metrics: BLEU , BLEURT (Sellam et al., 2020), the average length of the outputs and the diversity scores based on the proportion of unique n-grams over the total number of n-grams.

answer_4.quote: We also conduct two human evaluations in which model outputs are rated in terms of correctness while the errors are categorized.
answer_4.guideline: We ask the annotators to rate the correctness of each system response, using a 5-point Likert scale (i.e., 5-completely correct; 4-mostly correct, has minor and acceptable errors; 3-borderline, has both correct and incorrect information, nothing outweighs the other; 2-mostly incorrect, but still has correct information; 1-completely incorrect).
